name: Astera Labs
thesis: Astera Labs sells PCIe, CXL and Ethernet connectivity chips for AI racks; Q2 revenue was $392M (+105% y/y). It fell 11.1% on Oct 22 in the chip selloff (SOX -6.7%) and closed Oct 23 at $257.16, down 11.3% since Oct 21 and 33% below the Oct 7 close of $382.25. No company news found.
risks: A beta near 3.8 means 10% days on sector headlines alone; Meta's Q3 filing showed $810B of future lease and contract commitments, which fed worries about debt-funded AI build-outs.
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29 US (Oct 29-30 AEDT); Q3 results Nov 3 after US close, call 4:30pm ET (08:30 AEDT Wed Nov 4).

name: Broadcom
thesis: Broadcom supplies custom AI accelerators (Google, Meta, OpenAI) plus Ethernet networking and VMware. It held up better than most chips, -4.3% on Oct 22, closing Oct 23 at $321.68 (-4.8% since Oct 21). Meta's Q3 capex of $34.9B supports custom-silicon volume.
risks: Broadcom is arranging financing for OpenAI's chip purchases, so worries about debt-funded AI build-outs hit it directly; Meta's Q3 operating cash ($32.8B) did not cover capex ($34.9B).
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29 US (Oct 29-30 AEDT); Q4 FY26 results around Dec 10 (not yet confirmed).

name: Celestica
thesis: Celestica builds 800G/1.6T networking switches, servers and storage for hyperscalers; it guided Q3 to $5.3-5.6B revenue and $2.88-3.08 EPS (consensus about $5.44B and $2.97) and 2026 to $20.5B. It fell 11.7% on Oct 22 and closed Oct 23 at $260.01, down 14.6% since Oct 21, going into tonight's report.
risks: Single-digit hardware margins and a few hyperscaler customers; 2027 targets at the investor day will be judged against fears of a capex digestion year. CEO and CFO sold shares in the past three months.
catalyst: Q3 results Mon Oct 26 after US close (about 07:15 AEDT Tue Oct 27); call and Investor Day Tue Oct 27, 8:00am ET (23:00 AEDT Tue Oct 27).

name: Credo Technology
thesis: Credo sells active electrical cables (AECs), optical DSPs and retimers; fiscal Q1 2027 revenue was $479M (+115% y/y). It fell 19.2% over Oct 22-23 to $147.29 after MaxLinear said on its Oct 22 call it will target 20-30% of 1.6T AECs within a couple of years (it puts Credo's share at 93-99%), and third-party research flagged slower 1.6T rollouts. Conviction cut to low until fiscal Q2 shows the 1.6T ramp.
risks: A credible second source in AECs would hit pricing from fiscal 2028; a few hyperscalers drive most revenue, and the CEO and CTO have been selling under 10b5-1 plans.
catalyst: Fiscal Q2 2027 quarter ends about Oct 31; results early December (date not announced).

name: SK hynix ADR
thesis: SK hynix is the leading HBM supplier to Nvidia and the number-two DRAM maker. The ADR fell 8.1% on Oct 22, then rose 4.1% on Oct 23 to $137.02 after SK hynix dropped plans to list its US NAND unit Solidigm on Nasdaq, following shareholder backlash. Seoul shares closed Oct 23 at KRW 1,277,000 (+4.4%). Q3 on Oct 28 is the test.
risks: CXMT closing the density gap would pressure DRAM prices from 2027; the KOSPI fell about 19% in a month and Lam flagged equipment supply limits that could slow memory capacity adds.
catalyst: Q3 results and call Wed Oct 28, 9:00am KST (11:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28); Samsung full Q3 results Oct 29.

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: Bloom makes solid-oxide fuel cells for onsite data-centre power. Q3 revenue was a record $1.236B (+138% y/y), product revenue +179%, adjusted EPS $0.94 vs $0.69 expected, and 2026 guidance was raised a third time to $4.4-4.6B (from $3.9-4.2B). The stock fell 19% over Oct 22-23 to $193.30 on Q3 free cash flow of -$181M and the AI selloff, so forward P/E is about 40x vs 78x on Sep 30. Upgraded to accumulate.
risks: Capex of $153M (from $12M) to double capacity turned Q3 cash flow negative; delivery depends on Oracle and Brookfield sites arriving on time, and the stock moves 8-11% on sector days.
catalyst: Oracle Jupiter permit Nov 23; 2027 guidance and backlog figure with Q4 results (February).

name: GE Vernova
thesis: GE Vernova builds gas turbines, grid equipment and wind for the power build-out; Q2 orders rose 88% y/y and backlog is $176B. It fell 10.6% on Oct 22 with AI-power names after Meta's results, closing Oct 23 at $815.00, down 12.0% since Oct 21 and about 31% below the June 30 record of $1,174.86. No company news; BofA's Q3 preview (orders about +44% y/y, $1,310 target) stands.
risks: Q2 EPS missed ($2.47 vs $3.17) and wind still loses money, so another margin miss on Oct 28 would test the multiple; the stock is below its 50- and 200-day averages.
catalyst: Q3 results Wed Oct 28, webcast 7:30am ET (22:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: Vertiv
thesis: Vertiv sells power, thermal and liquid-cooling gear for data centres; it guided Q3 sales to $3.65-3.85B and lifted FY26 EPS to $6.65-6.75. It fell 7.8% on Oct 22 with AI-infrastructure names and closed Oct 23 at $194.32, down 8.4% since Oct 21; no company news found.
risks: The stock trades on the 2027 hyperscaler-capex debate rather than guidance, and price competition in liquid cooling is rising.
catalyst: Q3 results Wed Oct 28 before US open; call 11:00am ET (02:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29).

name: Robinhood
thesis: Robinhood is a retail brokerage adding prediction markets, perpetual futures and Robinhood Agents; Q2 revenue was $1.31B (+32%). Preliminary September data to Sep 24 showed about $267B equity volume, 234M options contracts and 4.4B event contracts. It closed Oct 23 at $95.07, down 6.7% since Oct 21 in the tech selloff.
risks: Revenue tracks crypto and equity volumes, and September crypto notional of about $17B (to Sep 24) is soft, so Q3 depends on options and event contracts.
catalyst: Q3 results and full September operating data Tue Oct 27 after close, video call 5pm ET (08:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: MercadoLibre runs Latin America's largest marketplace, logistics network and Mercado Pago; Q2 net revenue was $10.2B (+50% y/y) while operating income fell 17%. It closed Oct 23 at $1,810.15, down 2.4% since Oct 21. Brazil's Oct 25 runoff was still undeclared at last check: TSE had Lula 50.14% vs Flavio Bolsonaro 49.86% with about half counted, after the lead changed hands several times.
risks: Prediction markets had Lula about 91% to win late in the count; a Lula win would unwind part of the election premium in Brazilian assets. Margins are being absorbed by the credit book and logistics.
catalyst: TSE declaration and US open Mon Oct 26 (00:30 AEDT Tue Oct 27); Q3 results Nov 4 (provisional).

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Cloudflare runs a global edge network selling security, CDN, zero-trust and the Workers developer platform; Q2 revenue was $696M (+36%) and it guided Q3 to $736-737M. It closed Oct 23 at $325.73 (+7.3% that day on target raises), up 6.0% since Oct 21 while chips fell.
risks: The stock has had 38 moves of more than 5% in a year and now sits close to the consensus target, so Q3 has to beat and raise.
catalyst: Q3 results Thu Nov 5 after US close, call 5:00pm ET (09:00 AEDT Fri Nov 6).

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Sea runs Shopee, Monee (digital finance) and Garena across Southeast Asia and Brazil; Q2 revenue was $7.79B (+48%). After the Oct 20 memo on launching Sea Cloud and weighing a Monee IPO, it kept falling to $74.63 on Oct 23, below the prior 52-week low of $77.05 and 21% under the Oct 16 level. No new company news found.
risks: A new cloud business adds spending with no disclosed budget while Shopee fights TikTok Shop, Temu and Shein; DBS cut to Hold ($105) on 2027 margin worries. Weakest name on the list.
catalyst: Q3 results ~Nov 10 (TBC); any detail on Sea Cloud capex or Monee IPO timing.

name: Keyence
thesis: Keyence sells machine-vision, sensors and measurement gear direct to factories with industry-leading margins and no debt. It closed Oct 23 at JPY 78,380 (about US$500 at 156.84), down 3.1% since Oct 21, a much smaller fall than US chip names. Lam's record quarter and supply-constrained guide point to continued fab spending, a core end market.
risks: Orders follow the factory-capex cycle within a quarter, Q1 EPS slightly missed, and a stronger yen (BOJ meets Oct 29-30) cuts reported overseas revenue.
catalyst: Fiscal Q2 results Thu Oct 29 (time TBC, per StockAnalysis); BOJ decision Fri Oct 30.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: ASML is the only supplier of EUV lithography tools; Q3 sales were a record EUR 11.66B and it guided 2026 to EUR 44-45B, saying 2027-28 supply will not fully meet demand. The ADR fell 6.9% on Oct 22 when Lam said supply limits cut $300-400M from its Dec-quarter guide and could constrain the industry into 2027; it closed Oct 23 at $1,571.80 (-6.3% since Oct 21). Demand is not the issue.
risks: Semicap is priced for perfection and the SOX is in a bear market (26% off its June high); China is about 20% of ASML sales and export rules can change.
catalyst: Interim dividend EUR 1.88 payable Nov 4; Q4 results January (date TBC).

name: Teradyne
thesis: Teradyne makes test equipment for AI accelerators, HBM and mobile chips, plus Universal Robots; Q3 guidance is $1.20-1.30B revenue and $1.85-2.15 EPS (consensus about $1.26B and $2.05-2.08). It fell 10.6% on Oct 22 and closed Oct 23 at $308.85, down 10.6% since Oct 21. Options price a move of about 13% on the report.
risks: HBM test is a large part of the story, so a weak SK hynix or Samsung print the same week would hit it; test spend is lumpy and concentrated in a few customers.
catalyst: Q3 results Tue Oct 27 after US close (about 07:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28); call Wed Oct 28, 8:30am ET (23:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).
